overview.summary: A Stack is a linear data structure that follows the Last-In-First-Out (LIFO) principle.
learningObjectives: Implement a Stack using an Array or Linked List.
Recognize problems that require reversing order or matching pairs.
overview.interviewRelevance: Stacks are incredibly common in technical interviews, specifically for parsing strings, balancing parentheses, and tracking history.

paragraphs: Think of a stack of plates at a buffet. You can only take the plate that is right on top.
When a new plate is washed, it is placed on the very top of the stack. The last plate added is the first one taken. This is LIFO.
realWorldHook.ahaMoment: A Stack inherently reverses the order of elements. Whatever went in last, comes out first!

definition.technicalDefinition: A Stack is an abstract data type that serves as a collection of elements, with two principal operations: push (adds an element) and pop (removes the most recently added element).

vocabulary.definition: Insert an element onto the top of the stack.
Remove the top element from the stack.
Look at the top element without removing it.
A stack that maintains elements in non-increasing or non-decreasing order.

keyProperties: O(n) search (since you only have direct access to the top).
Can be implemented via Arrays or Linked Lists.

metaphor: A tube of tennis balls. You can only put a ball in the top, and take a ball from the top.
mentalModel.clickSentence: Use a Stack whenever you need to 'go back' or process the most recent thing first.

memoryDescription: If implemented with an Array, the 'top' of the stack is just the end of the array.
If implemented with a Linked List, the 'top' of the stack is the Head of the list.

definitionCode.python:
stack = []
stack.append(1)  # Push
top = stack.pop() # Pop

operations.name: Pop
operations.visualNote: The top element is pulled off the stack.

patternTemplate.whenToUse: Parsing expressions, checking valid parentheses, tracking previous states (undo buttons), or implementing DFS.

recognitionQuiz.problemStatement: You need to implement the 'Undo' button in a text editor.
recognitionQuiz.explanation: Undo requires reverting the MOST RECENT action first. This perfectly matches the Last-In-First-Out (LIFO) model of a Stack.

examples.title: Valid Parentheses
examples.problemStatement: Given a string containing just the characters '(', ')', '{', '}', '[' and ']', determine if the input string is valid.
steps: If it's an opening bracket, push to stack.
If it's a closing bracket, pop from stack and check if they match.
Stack must be empty at the end.
examples.rationale: The stack perfectly tracks the most recent unclosed bracket, ensuring it gets closed first.

conceptQuiz.question: Which principle does a Stack follow?
conceptQuiz.explanation: LIFO. The last item pushed onto the stack is the first item popped off. (Note: FILO is technically identical, but LIFO is the standard industry term).

conceptQuiz.question: What happens if you pop an empty stack?
conceptQuiz.explanation: Attempting to pop from an empty stack is called a Stack Underflow.
